title: Cosmetics Manufacturer Registration in Korea: Facilities, Documents & Procedure | YouSun Administrative Agency
lead: A business that manufactures all or part of a cosmetic product in Korea must register as a cosmetics manufacturer (화장품제조업) with the Regional Office of Food and Drug Safety (지방식품의약품안전청) covering the manufacturing site. It needs a work area, storage area, testing room and other facilities plus the representative's medical certificates, and the application form sets a processing period of 15 days. A brand that outsources production and only sells under its own name registers as a cosmetics responsible seller (화장품책임판매업) instead.
summary: Who: businesses that manufacture cosmetics directly, manufacture them under contract, or do primary packaging (secondary packaging or labelling alone is excluded).
Filed with: the Regional Office of Food and Drug Safety covering the manufacturing site.

Key requirements: work area, storage area, testing room and quality testing equipment (partly omitted when only part of the process is done or testing is outsourced), and no disqualification of the representative.
Documents: cosmetics manufacturer registration application, representative's medical certificates (no mental illness, no narcotics addiction), facility specification.
Processing: 15 days per the application form; change registration within 30 days of the change.

sections.body:
Under the Cosmetics Act (화장품법), a cosmetics manufacturer is a business that manufactures all or part of a cosmetic product; processes limited to secondary packaging or labelling are excluded. There are three sub-types: (1) manufacturing cosmetics directly (2) manufacturing cosmetics under contract for another company (3) primary packaging only. Primary packaging means the container in direct contact with the contents, so a business that only fills contents into containers still needs cosmetics manufacturer registration.

By contrast, a brand that has an OEM or ODM partner produce its products and only distributes and sells them under its own name registers as a cosmetics responsible seller, not as a manufacturer. A business that both makes and sells its products registers as both, and the manufacturer application has a box asking whether the business also operates as a responsible seller.

sections.h2: What are the facility standards for a cosmetics manufacturer?
sections.body:
An applicant must have: (1) a work area with facilities that keep out rodents, insects and dust, work benches and other equipment needed for manufacturing, and dust removal facilities in rooms where powder is handled (2) a storage area for raw materials, packaging materials and products (3) a testing room for quality testing of raw materials, packaging materials and products (4) facilities and equipment needed for quality testing.

There are two exceptions. A manufacturer doing only part of the process may omit facilities and equipment other than those that process needs. And a manufacturer that outsources quality testing to a Research Institute of Public Health and Environment, a manufacturer with a testing room, a designated cosmetics testing and inspection institution or the Korea Pharmaceutical Traders Association (한국의약품수출입협회) may omit the testing room and testing equipment. The manufacturing facilities may also be used to make products other than cosmetics unless there is a risk of cross-contamination.

sections.h2: What are the disqualification grounds for cosmetics manufacturer registration?
sections.body:
Registration is not available to: (1) a person with a mental illness (except a person a psychiatrist recognises as suitable to be a cosmetics manufacturer) (2) a person under adult guardianship (3) a person addicted to narcotics (4) a person sentenced to imprisonment without labour or heavier for violating the Cosmetics Act or the Act on Special Measures for the Control of Public Health Crimes (보건범죄 단속에 관한 특별조치법) whose sentence has not been completed or remitted (5) a person on probation for a suspended sentence of that level for those violations (6) a person whose registration was cancelled or whose business was closed less than one year ago.

The mental illness and narcotics addiction grounds apply only to cosmetics manufacturers, not to responsible sellers, which is why only the manufacturer application requires medical certificates for these two points.

sections.h2: What documents are required for cosmetics manufacturer registration?
sections.body:
The cosmetics manufacturer registration application (electronic filing available) is filed with: (1) a doctor's certificate that the applicant (the representative, for a corporation) is not a person with a mental illness, or a psychiatrist's certificate that they are suitable as a cosmetics manufacturer (2) a doctor's certificate that they are not addicted to narcotics (3) a facility specification.

The applicant does not submit the corporate register; the regional office checks it through shared administrative information. The application states the applicant's details, the trade name and location of the manufacturing site, the manufacturing type, and whether the business also operates as a responsible seller.

sections.h2: What is the procedure and how long does it take?
sections.body:
(1) Decide the manufacturing type (direct, contract or primary packaging) → (2) secure and fit out the site and decide whether to outsource quality testing → (3) obtain the representative's medical certificates → (4) file the application and attachments → (5) review and supplementation → (6) issuance of the cosmetics manufacturer registration certificate.

The application form sets a processing period of 15 days. When the requirements are met, the office records the registration number and date, the manufacturer's name, the trade name, the site location and the manufacturing type in the register and issues the certificate. Time for site fit-out, certificates and supplementation is separate from the processing period.

sections.h2: Which changes require a change registration after registering?
sections.body:
Change registration is required for: (1) a change of manufacturer (the representative, for a corporation) (2) a change of trade name (the corporate name, for a corporation) (3) a change of site location (4) a change of manufacturing type. File the cosmetics manufacturer change registration application with the registration certificate within 30 days of the change (90 days for a location change caused by administrative district reorganisation).

A new representative submits the two medical certificates, and a business transfer also needs proof of the transfer. Relocation requires a facility specification, and if the move changes the competent office, you file with the regional office covering the new location. A primary packaging registrant that switches to or adds direct or contract manufacturing also submits a facility specification. The change registration form sets a processing period of 15 days.

Failing to register a change leads to administrative sanctions; for an unregistered change of site location or manufacturing type, the first-violation standard is a one-month suspension of manufacturing.

sections.h2: What must a cosmetics manufacturer comply with after registration?
sections.body:
A cosmetics manufacturer must: (1) follow the responsible seller's guidance, supervision and requests under the quality control standards (2) prepare and keep the manufacturing control standard, product standard, manufacturing control records and quality control records (electronic form included) (3) keep the site, facilities and equipment hygienic and protected from contamination (4) inspect facilities and equipment regularly and maintain them (5) keep hazardous items out of the work area and prevent harmful substances from leaking or being released (6) submit items needed for quality control to the responsible seller (7) carry out the necessary tests, inspections or assays from receipt of raw materials to release of finished products (8) supervise any contractor used for manufacturing or quality testing and keep its records. Breaching these duties is punishable by a fine of up to KRW 2 million.

Where facilities fail the facility standards or are worn or damaged so that safety and quality are at risk, the authority can order repairs or ban use of the facilities until repairs are done. CGMP (우수화장품 제조 및 품질관리기준, Korean cosmetics good manufacturing practice) is a recommended standard rather than a registration requirement; compliant facility assessment is covered on the CGMP page.

sections.h2: What can an administrative agent help with?
sections.body: On your authorization, YouSun Administrative Agency determines the manufacturing type, pre-checks the facility standards, prepares the registration application and facility specification, files with the competent Regional Office of Food and Drug Safety, responds to supplementation requests and prepares change registrations and closure or suspension reports. Facility construction, quality testing and on-site CGMP quality consulting are not provided. Work restricted by other laws cannot be handled, and court representation is outside the scope of an administrative agent. Whether registration is granted is decided by the competent authority.

faq.q: Is a cosmetics manufacturer licensed or registered?
faq.a: It is a registration under the Cosmetics Act. A change registration is also required when the representative, trade name, site location or manufacturing type changes.

faq.q: Can one manufacturing site make products other than cosmetics?
faq.a: Yes, cosmetics manufacturing facilities may be used to make other products, but not where there is a risk of cross-contamination between products.

faq.q: Does a contract manufacturer have to share its manufacturing records with the brand?
faq.a: The items needed for quality control from the manufacturing control standard, product standard and records must be submitted to the responsible seller. This is not required where the manufacturer and responsible seller are the same, or where the manufacturer designs, develops and produces the product and the items are trade secrets under their contract within a range that does not affect quality and safety management.

faq.q: Do we need CGMP compliant status before registering as a cosmetics manufacturer?
faq.a: No. The registration requirements are the facility standards and no disqualification; CGMP is a recommended standard. Manufacturers that follow it may receive technical and training support, advice, and support for repairing facilities and equipment.

faq.q: What happens if we manufacture cosmetics without registration?
faq.a: Operating without cosmetics manufacturer registration is punishable by imprisonment of up to 3 years or a fine of up to KRW 30 million, and both may be imposed together. The same applies to registration or change registration obtained by false or fraudulent means.

faq.q: Do we need to report a suspension or closure of the site?
faq.a: Yes. Closure, suspension and resumption after suspension are reported to the competent Regional Office of Food and Drug Safety, except a suspension of less than one month. Acceptance of a closure or suspension report is notified within 7 days of receipt.

citations.text: Cosmetics manufacturer: a business that manufactures all or part of cosmetics, excluding secondary packaging or labelling only
Sub-types: direct manufacturing, contract manufacturing, primary packaging only
Application with two medical certificates and a facility specification, filed with the regional office covering the site
Work area, storage area, testing room and testing equipment, partly omitted for partial processes or outsourced testing
Four change registration items, within 30 days (90 days for district reorganisation)
Mental illness and narcotics addiction grounds apply to manufacturers only
